name: JSMA
tagline: Jacobian-based Saliency Map Attack: greedy white-box attack that flips the most-salient input features two at a time toward the least-likely class.
pseudocode:
1. Pick target $t = \arg\min_c p_c(x)$ (least-likely class).
2. Compute saliency $S_{ij}(x,t) = \partial p_t / \partial x_{ij} \cdot |\sum_{c\neq t}\partial p_c/\partial x_{ij}|$ when signs match, else 0.
3. Select feature pair $(i^*, j^*)$ with highest joint saliency.
4. Push both to extreme value $\theta=1$.
5. Repeat for $\lceil \text{pixels}/2\rceil$ iterations (i.e. $\gamma = \text{pixels}/(CHW)$ caps total perturbed features).
6. Return adversarial image, clipped to [0,1].
diff_from_baseline: Papernot et al., EuroS&P 2016 — Jacobian-based Saliency Map Attack. Targeted-only white-box attack via torchattacks; with least-likely-class targeting and γ tuned so that ≤ pixels features are flipped, satisfying the L0 budget.

name: OnePixel (DE)
tagline: Differential-Evolution black-box attack: searches a few-pixel coordinate+RGB perturbation that maximises misclassification.
pseudocode:
1. Encode each candidate perturbation as a vector of (x, y, r, g, b)×pixels values.
2. Initialise a population of size popsize with random spatial+colour entries.
3. for `steps` generations: mutate via DE (parent + F·(p1 − p2)), crossover, and select if classifier confidence on true class drops.
4. Score on the model in batches of size `inf_batch=128`.
5. Return the best perturbed image found within the L0 budget.
diff_from_baseline: Su, Vargas & Sakurai 2017/2019 — One Pixel Attack via differential evolution. Black-box, derivative-free baseline that natively respects spatial-pixel L0 budgets.

name: Pixle (patch-swap)
tagline: Black-box patch-swap attack: replaces small image patches with pixels copied from elsewhere in the image, iterated with restarts.
pseudocode:
1. for restart $= 1\ldots R$:
2.  for it $= 1\ldots\text{max\_iterations}$:
3.   pick a random patch of size $(x\_dim, y\_dim)$ in the image and a random source location.
4.   copy source pixels into target patch (random pixel mapping).
5.   keep the swap if the model's loss on the true label increases; otherwise revert (`update_each_iteration=False` means apply only the best at the end).
6. Return the best adversarial image.
diff_from_baseline: Pomponi, Scardapane & Uncini 2022 — Pixle. Score-based black-box attack that perturbs by re-arranging existing pixels; produces sparse, in-distribution colour edits.

name: Sparse-RS (L0)
tagline: SOTA black-box L0 attack: random search that swaps subsets of perturbed pixels and resamples binary RGB colors, accepted by margin loss.
pseudocode:
1. Initialise: pick a random set $\mathcal{B}$ of $\epsilon$ spatial pixels, fill with binary $\{0,1\}^C$ colors.
2. Compute margin loss $L = f_y(x) - \max_{c\neq y} f_c(x)$.
3. for it $= 1\ldots n_{queries}$:
4.  draw a swap fraction $p(\text{it})$ via the Croce et al. schedule, propose to revert $\lceil p\,\epsilon \rceil$ pixels and perturb the same number of new pixels with fresh binary colors.
5.  evaluate $L'$; accept if $L'$ improves or if margin already $<0$, swap mask indices accordingly.
6. Stop early when all margins are negative; return $x_{best}$.
diff_from_baseline: Croce et al., AAAI 2022 — Sparse-RS. Versatile query-efficient sparse random search; current black-box L0 SOTA. Inlined from the official rs_attacks.py because torchattacks lacks a Sparse-RS implementation.

name: SparseFool
tagline: Linear-approximation white-box L0 attack: iteratively projects DeepFool's hyperplane to a few coordinates per step.
pseudocode:
1. Run DeepFool to find the minimum L2 perturbation $r^*$ to cross the closest decision hyperplane.
2. Approximate the boundary linearly: solve a sparse box-constrained projection that touches the hyperplane while modifying as few pixels as possible (with overshoot $1+\eta$).
3. Apply the resulting sparse perturbation; clip to $[0,1]$.
4. Repeat up to `steps`=20 iterations, scaling by $\lambda=3$.
5. Return $x_{adv}$.
diff_from_baseline: Modas, Moosavi-Dezfooli & Frossard, CVPR 2019 — SparseFool. White-box DeepFool-based L0 attack that finds minimum-pixel perturbations via iterative sparse linearised projections.
